clue.text: Give retrospective validity to second appointment

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
an appointment fixed for a time

explanation.surface: Someone gets a second appointment approved after the fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating a document earlier than its signing makes it take effect from a past point.

clue.text: Perform again on island — it's off France

parts.note: bis is the call for an encore, asking performers to repeat a piece
a cay is a low coral island or sandbank

explanation.surface: A troupe gives an encore on an island off the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Biscay lies along the western Atlantic coast of France.

clue.text: Box heavyweight after initially cutting and running

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the finished word
initially points at the opening letter of each of the three following words

parts.note: the first letters of these three words
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer cuts and runs from the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a verb about the heavyweight's sport; it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard container for goods such as milk or eggs is a kind of packaging box.

clue.text: Fabulous figure? About right — four see without doubt

parts.note: informally a demon is someone brilliant, as in a demon bowler

indicators.note: about means going around, so one item surrounds the next

parts.note: the Bishop of Ely's diocese, a see

explanation.surface: A cryptic musing on a mythical figure and four sightings of something certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous figure' reads as a mythical creature, but the two words are clued separately. A see is a bishop's diocese; the Cambridgeshire cathedral city is the setters' favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrative can mean serving to prove conclusively, so acting this way leaves no room for uncertainty.

clue.text: Tyre part ultimately deficient, not fully prepared

indicators.note: not fully means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter
ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: A worn, deficient tyre on a car that was not properly prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The patterned rubber surface of a tyre that grips the road is one section of it.

clue.text: Film extremely prudish, cosy? Wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests things put in a mistaken order, so the letters must be rearranged
extremely means at the extremes, so the word's two end letters are taken

explanation.surface: A film critic finds a movie both prudish and cosy, and disapproves.
explanation.walkthrough: Both end letters of 'prudish' join the four letters of 'cosy' in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller with its famous shower scene is a celebrated example of a movie.

clue.text: Adapting ways and means, not initially deft, for love?

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter, so the opening letter is dropped
adapting means reshaping, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone cleverly adapts their methods, asking whether it is all done for love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis scores; SWEET FANNY ADAMS is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means zero in scoring, and this slang phrase likewise means absolutely nothing, nil.

clue.text: About time a series of items is mentioned — that should expedite things

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word is judged by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a series of items set down one after another

explanation.surface: An impatient remark that listing everything at last should speed up the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance or person that speeds a reaction or prompts change makes things happen more quickly.

clue.text: In cold fog, eyeless, he fusses?

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A man stumbling blind in cold fog grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and 'eyeless' break the surface but are ignored in the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy, conservative old person who grumbles about change is the stock picture of this phrase.

clue.text: Pro's small instrument

explanation.surface: A professional musician owns a little instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Pro’s' as 'pro is': pro is short for prostitute here, not professional.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a prostitute or promiscuous woman, which slang shortens to pro.

clue.text: Boss welcomes training group

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one word holds the other inside it

explanation.surface: A manager greets a group arriving for training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training group' looks like one phrase; 'training' belongs to the wordplay and 'group' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of seven things together is a numerical group, from the Greek for seven.

clue.text: Natural drinking place at bottom of terrace

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pub with drinkers out on the terrace seems quite natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn qualities are present from birth, so they come naturally rather than being learned.

clue.text: Decorate a sleeping area, new, for married

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps out another

explanation.surface: Instructions to spruce up a dormitory for newlyweds.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish something with ornaments is to make it more beautiful, a synonym for decorating it.

clue.text: Academic with answer: inform old sculptor

explanation.surface: A professor who has the answer briefs someone about an old sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' does double duty: it supplies O and qualifies the sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine Renaissance master who carved the bronze David lived in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Unlikely American has regularly visited scene in capital

parts.note: as in a tall story, hard to believe

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the next word is kept

explanation.surface: An improbable American keeps returning to the scene of something in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visited' only links the wordplay; 'regularly' looks like it describes the visits but picks letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the seat of government of the US state of Florida, its capital city.

clue.text: John, King, brought over Queen — she's worth seeing

indicators.note: in a down entry brought over places the earlier pieces above the next one

explanation.surface: A royal court scene: John and the King escort the Queen, a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: John is a toilet in slang, a LOO in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person, informally, is someone pleasant to look at.

clue.text: Dishes, say, good, associated with luxury transport

explanation.surface: Fine dishes are said to go with arriving in a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: These Chinese deep-fried pancake rolls are served as plates of food on a menu.

clue.text: Tolerate for most part emperor's writer

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to brook is to put up with

explanation.surface: Putting up with an emperor's author, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita Brookner was an English novelist who won the Booker Prize for Hotel du Lac.

clue.text: Relevant to include retrospective business article — "North Sea in past"?

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other
retrospective means looking back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A retrospective feature on business, with a headline about the North Sea's history.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a quiz-style question: this was an old name for the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Older maps named the stretch of water between Britain and the Continent after Germany.

clue.text: Move quickly about foreign pal's kinsfolk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: French for friend; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Rushing to see a foreign friend's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives as a group make up one's household and blood relations, the same thing as kin.

clue.text: Not showing judgment EU wins after review

indicators.note: a review reworks what is examined, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A political verdict: a European Union victory after an appeal was poor judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish or ill-advised conduct lacks good sense, which is lacking judgment.

clue.text: Commodious state — son is more relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters are free to fall into another order

explanation.surface: A spacious home, where a son feels more at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodious means spacious, so the condition of being commodious is having plenty of space.

clue.text: Freedom to develop resort supported by Church

indicators.note: in a down entry supported by puts the first piece on top of the next

explanation.surface: A resort backed by the Church has room to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given room or scope lets someone grow and act without restriction.

clue.text: Not for first time opposed to abandoning street

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so those letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Residents once again object to losing their street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done once more happens a second time, so it is not the first occasion.

clue.text: Tree, large, next to popular animal home

explanation.surface: A big tree beside a favourite animal's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime, a broad-leaved shade tree, goes by this other common name.

clue.text: Ritual greeting interrupted by a painter with drink

indicators.note: interrupted by means broken into, so the other pieces sit inside the word

explanation.surface: A ceremonial welcome cut short by an artist with a drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ritual' looks like an adjective for the greeting but is the definition, of the Japanese ritual suicide.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese samurai's ceremonial self-disembowelment was a ritual act of honour.

clue.text: In Sargasso Sea at first carrier drifts off course

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others
at first points at the opening letter of each word before it

explanation.surface: A ship in the Sargasso Sea drifts off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests an aircraft carrier at sea, but it is a humble tea tray.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander from the proper path or route is to deviate, as a ship drifting does.

clue.text: Gregory's reckoning Yeltsin not in maybe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Gregorian calendar dating system
second meaning, cryptic: Yeltsin without IN leaves five letters which a fresh arrangement could turn into a common word for manner

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works backwards: read the answer as an instruction, a new arrangement of STYLE, and it gives YELTS, which is Yeltsin missing IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates under Pope Gregory XIII's calendar reform, adopted in Britain in 1752, are called this.
